name: Core Data (used directly instead of SwiftData)
verdict_reason: Developer reports from late 2023 put SwiftData far behind Core Data: fetches of about 1 ms in Core Data taking about 20 ms, and a 30,000-row import taking 90+ seconds against 3 seconds. These are anecdotes without code or build settings, and one developer saw much less lag on the iOS 18 beta, though memory stayed at double Core Data's.
tier_reason: Forum and blog reports with numbers but no published code, device, OS build or compiler settings.
claimed_speedup: Fetch/query: 'around 1ms in CoreData' vs 'around 20ms' in SwiftData; creating ~30,000 @Model instances: '90+ seconds' vs 3 seconds without the @Model macro and in the earlier Core Data version; iOS 18 beta: SwiftData 'memory usage was still double that of CoreData'.
workload: Instantiating @Model objects (15 scalar properties) from a ~30,000-line CSV; fetch/query calls profiled with Instruments in an app migrating from Core Data.
one_liner: Using Core Data directly skips SwiftData's model layer; developers report fetches about 20x faster, but only anecdotally.
how_it_is_fast: SwiftData sits on top of Core Data: every @Model instance carries macro-generated accessors, a backing-data object and an observation registrar, and a reply in the same thread says its in-memory storage keeps values in a Dictionary. NSManagedObject subclasses skip that layer, and Core Data adds batch insert, update and delete requests that write without creating objects at all.
use_it_when: Bulk imports or tight fetch loops where per-object model overhead shows up in profiles
Apps that still support iOS 16 or earlier
Work that suits NSBatchInsertRequest and other batch requests
skip_it_when: Small data sets where the per-object overhead is not measurable
Teams that value SwiftData's macro models and @Query more than raw speed
caveats: No device, OS build or Debug/Release setting is given; a reply asks whether the poster used a Release build
Reports date from iOS 17.x; SwiftData internals changed in later releases and one developer reports much less lag on the iOS 18 beta
No controlled, reproducible SwiftData vs Core Data benchmark was found
tradeoffs: Older API: NSManagedObject subclasses, contexts and threading rules
More boilerplate in SwiftUI than @Model and @Query

evidence.quote: This takes around 90+ seconds to complete.
In previous version of my app using core data loop took 3 seconds also.
Profiling with the instrument showed that operations (e.g. Fetch/Query) that took around 1ms in CoreData take around 20ms now.
I did, and while there was much less lag, memory usage was still double that of CoreData.
